solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: From which Spooner might have phoned water regulators?

indicators.note: the Reverend Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the phrase must have its initial sounds exchanged

parts.words: From which Spooner might have phoned
parts.note: a call box is a public telephone booth, the place you phone from; swapping its opening sounds gives the regulators

explanation.surface: A mischievous question about a man ringing up the plumbing.
explanation.walkthrough: Swap the C of CALL and the B of BOX to get BALL COCKS. A call box is a British phone booth.
explanation.definitionFit: A ballcock is the floating valve in a cistern that shuts off the flow when the tank is full.

clue.text: Puff of cloud, first sign of blizzard

parts.note: to cloud a view is to blur it

indicators.note: the first sign of a word is its opening letter, so only that is kept

parts.note: opening letter of the storm word

explanation.surface: A wisp of cloud heralds a coming snowstorm.
explanation.definitionFit: A puff is a piece of promotional praise, such as the publisher's text on a book jacket.

clue.text: Five years of lechery and alcohol

parts.note: a spirit, as an example of alcohol

explanation.surface: Half a decade of debauchery and drinking.
explanation.definitionFit: A lustrum is a Roman term for a period of half a decade, originally marked by a purification ceremony.

clue.text: Local news broadcast ultimately betrays inexperience

indicators.note: to broadcast seed is to scatter it, so the letters are scattered and rearranged
ultimately points to the final letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A regional bulletin ends up showing how green its reporters are.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' looks natural next to news, but it is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Callow means young and lacking worldly experience, so the noun names that immaturity.

clue.text: Musician's twice shunning hemp plant

indicators.note: shunning means avoiding, so those letters are kept out of the longer word

parts.note: bis is the musical direction to repeat a passage

explanation.surface: A performer twice turns down the hemp plant.
explanation.walkthrough: CANNABIS without BIS leaves CANNA; the clue reads as wordplay then definition, with 'plant' doing double duty in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Canna is a genus of tropical flowering plants with bright blooms, often called canna lilies.

clue.text: One above criticism landed in barge

indicators.note: in says one word is placed inside the other

parts.note: a scow is a flat-bottomed barge

explanation.surface: Someone untouchable has come ashore on a flat boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Landed' looks like a verb about arriving; it is the old adjective meaning owning acres.
explanation.definitionFit: A sacred cow is an institution or idea held to be immune from questioning or attack.

clue.text: One included in his progeny?

indicators.note: included in says the letters sit inside the run of words that follows

parts.note: letters running across the two words

explanation.surface: Asking whether someone counts among a man's offspring.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both the hiding place and the definition. Sprog is British slang for a child.
explanation.definitionFit: A child is one member of a person's offspring, and this slang word means exactly a youngster.

clue.text: Try to find faithful person by word of mouth

indicators.note: word of mouth means spoken, so the word is heard rather than spelt

parts.note: a Sikh is an adherent of the Sikh faith

explanation.surface: Hunting for a loyal friend through personal recommendation.
explanation.definitionFit: To seek is to look for or search out something, the same as attempting to locate it.

clue.text: Composer runs former East German province, largely

parts.note: R is the cricket abbreviation for runs
Ossi is the German nickname for someone from the old GDR
Northern Ireland is called the Province; its abbreviation is most of its name cut away

explanation.surface: A musician hurries through a region of the old GDR.
explanation.definitionFit: Gioachino Rossini was the Italian who wrote operas such as The Barber of Seville.

clue.text: Font choice upset grand poet

indicators.note: something upset is knocked over and disordered, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A typeface selection dismays an eminent versifier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Font' suggests typefaces; here it is the baptismal font, and the parents choose this sponsor for the christening.
explanation.definitionFit: Parents select sponsors who stand at the baptismal basin to make promises for the baby.

clue.text: Character oddly mislaid bus pass in west side of London

indicators.note: the odd-numbered letters are lost, leaving only the even ones

parts.note: second, fourth, sixth and eighth letters

indicators.note: on a map west is the left, so the left-hand half of the word is kept

parts.note: the left half of the city's name

explanation.surface: Someone loses their bus pass in west London.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'in' is part of the letter run, not a container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Upsilon is the twentieth letter of the Greek alphabet, and a letter is a character.

clue.text: Rumpled journalist chasing crew-cut Anglo-Saxon

indicators.note: cut says the word is shortened, losing its end
chasing means following behind, so this piece comes after the others

parts.note: AS is the abbreviation for Anglo-Saxon

explanation.surface: A dishevelled reporter pursues a shaven-headed Englishman of old.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Crew-cut' looks like a hairstyle; split it, and the crew loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Rumpled clothes are wrinkled and full of folds, just like creased fabric.

clue.text: Will lover possibly stop affair in due course?

parts.note: a do is a party or affair

explanation.surface: Would someone end a fling when the time comes?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Will' is Will Shakespeare, known as the Bard; the capital is disguised at the start of the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who idolises Shakespeare excessively is said to worship the Bard of Avon.

clue.text: Sanctimonious about unnatural desire

explanation.surface: A prig lectures on improper longings.
explanation.definitionFit: Pica is a medical condition involving cravings to eat non-food substances such as chalk or soil.

clue.text: Mob united with rebel force

parts.note: to mob is to crowd round, to press
U for United, as in football team names
to rise up is to rebel

explanation.surface: A crowd joins an insurgent army.
explanation.definitionFit: To pressurise someone is to coerce them into acting, the verb meaning compel.

clue.text: Publicist of legendary batsman (not British)

indicators.note: not says the bracketed letters are absent from the longer name

parts.note: Don Bradman, the great Australian cricketer
BR is an abbreviation for British

explanation.surface: The PR agent of a famous cricketer, not a Brit.
explanation.walkthrough: The bracket fits the surface, since Bradman was Australian.
explanation.definitionFit: An adman works in advertising, promoting products to the public, which is what a publicist does.

clue.text: The whole of humanity's enthralled by overblown plot

indicators.note: to be enthralled by something is to be held captive within it

explanation.surface: Everyone is gripped by a melodramatic storyline.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plot' sounds like a story; here it is a patch of land. An allotment is a rented garden plot in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: An allotment is a small piece of ground rented for growing vegetables, a type of plot.

clue.text: Rambling partner once joined up

explanation.surface: A former companion went walking and joined a group.
explanation.definitionFit: Excursive means digressive, wandering off the point, as discursive speech does.

clue.text: Hearing couple reserving hotel room and early bird breakfast?

indicators.note: reserving means keeping something held inside

explanation.surface: A pair booking a hotel room with an early breakfast deal.
explanation.walkthrough: Proverbially the early bird catches the worm, so the definition plays on a hotel's breakfast offer.
explanation.definitionFit: The saying has the early-rising bird catching a worm, its morning meal.

clue.text: Artist on streets breaking rules in ultimate provocation

indicators.note: breaking into something means getting inside it

parts.note: the law is a set of rules

indicators.note: in an across clue one piece set on another follows it

parts.note: ST twice, the abbreviation for street

explanation.surface: A painter on the streets flouting regulations as a final act of defiance.
explanation.definitionFit: The last straw is the final annoyance that makes something unbearable, from the straw that broke the camel's back.

clue.text: Sleep in hovel right behind deserted bathhouse

indicators.note: behind means coming after, placing this piece last
deserted means emptied, so the inner letters go and only the ends stay

explanation.surface: Bedding down in a shack behind an abandoned bathing house.
explanation.definitionFit: Slumber is a literary word for sleeping, both as noun and verb.

clue.text: Brushed last of locks and blubbed

indicators.note: last of points to the final letter of the next word

explanation.surface: Someone sweeps up the final hair clippings and sobs.
explanation.definitionFit: To sweep is to clean with a brush, so a floor swept has been brushed.

clue.text: Polite invalid accepting kiss for heroic deed

indicators.note: accepting means taking something in
invalid means unsound or not right, so the letters are reworked

parts.note: X is a kiss at the end of a letter

explanation.surface: A courteous patient takes a kiss as reward for bravery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Invalid' reads as a sick person; it is the adjective meaning unsound.
explanation.definitionFit: An exploit is a bold or daring feat, the kind of act admired as brave.

clue.text: Back of coat with skirt and hood

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter

parts.note: to skirt a coast is to hug it, keeping close

explanation.surface: An outfit of coat, skirt and hood.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hood' looks like clothing to match the coat; it is short for hoodlum.
explanation.definitionFit: A hood is American slang for a hoodlum, a violent criminal or gangster.

clue.text: Reveal top competitive rider

parts.note: a jumper is a sweater, a top in British usage

explanation.surface: Unveiling the leading equestrian contestant.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Top' reads as best; it is a garment.
explanation.definitionFit: Show jumpers ride horses over fences in timed competitive arena events.

clue.text: Most inferior hammer

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the poorest in quality
second meaning: to beat or defeat soundly

explanation.surface: The cheapest, shoddiest hammer in the shop.
explanation.definitionFit: The superlative of bad means lowest quality, and as a verb it means to thrash an opponent.

clue.text: Commit offence in pursuit of extremely rare hashish?

indicators.note: in pursuit means following, so this piece comes after
extremely means at the extremes, so only the end letters are kept

explanation.surface: Breaking the law in search of very scarce cannabis.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark flags that hashish is only one example of the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Hashish is cannabis resin, the sticky substance pressed from the plant, so it is an example.

clue.text: Burritos regularly providing energy

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, taking every other letter

parts.note: first, third, fifth and seventh letters

explanation.surface: Eating Mexican wraps often gives you a boost.
explanation.definitionFit: Brio is vigour and liveliness, a spirited vitality.

clue.text: Ban retired setter, boozer with zest

indicators.note: retired means withdrawn, going backwards

parts.note: a boozer is British slang for a pub

explanation.surface: Bar a retired compiler who drinks with gusto.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boozer' reads as a drinker; in British slang it is the pub itself.
explanation.definitionFit: An embargo is an official prohibition, especially on trade with a country.

clue.text: Our uni's shockingly dilapidated

indicators.note: shockingly suggests a jolt that throws things into disorder

explanation.surface: A student laments that their university is falling apart.
explanation.definitionFit: Ruinous can describe a building in ruins, decayed and falling down.

clue.text: Trunk and bunk turned round thus

indicators.note: turned round means facing the other way, read backwards

explanation.surface: A storage chest and a bed swapped around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Trunk' and 'bunk' suggest furniture; trunk is the body and bunk is nonsense.
explanation.definitionFit: The torso is the main part of the human body, excluding head and limbs.

clue.text: Seedy old Romeo ejected from theatre in outskirts of Malvern

indicators.note: in says the combined piece goes inside
outskirts are the edges, so only the outer letters are kept
ejected means thrown out, so that letter leaves the word

explanation.surface: An aged lothario thrown out of a playhouse in a Worcestershire spa town.
explanation.walkthrough: Malvern is an English town famous for its theatre festival.
explanation.definitionFit: Moth-eaten means shabby and worn out, as is something seedy and run-down.
